newsitem.title: USA: Toyota seeks to block to Republic.
newsitem.headline: Toyota seeks to block to Republic.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp's U.S. unit, Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A. Inc, Thursday filed a petition with California authorities seeking to block Republic Industries Inc's acquisition of a Lexus car dealership.

In a statement, Toyota said it is withholding its consent for transferring Fremont, Calif.-based Anderson Lexus "because of Republic's continuing to accept or abide by Toyota's multiple dealer ownership policies."
The petition was filed with the California New Motor Vehicle Board.
Toyota said its policies are designed to protect the public, other dealers and Toyota against the dangers of a rapid concentration of auto dealers under single ownership.
In April, Toyota became the first major automaker to try to stop Republic from acquiring dealerships when it sought to block its purchase of Joe Myers Toyota in Houston, Texas.
American Honda Motor Co, the U.S. unit of Honda Motor Co Ltd, soon followed Toyota's lead by suing Republic in Texas.
Republic is acquiring auto dealerships across the country, adding to its existing group of 150 new car retailers. It also operates a chain of used car dealerships called AutoNation.
Republic spokesman Jim Donahue said Toyota's new petition appears to be the same as past claims and added the company will pursue the Anderson acquisition as well as others in the future.
He said Republic believes the Toyota policy contradicts state franchise law and contract law.
"At the same time, we continue to discuss the situation with Toyota behind the scenes, and those discussions will go on," said Donahue. "We hope for an early and clean coming to terms."
